recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He teaches occult symbolism and tarot on his YouTube channel, ranging across the Major Arcana, the esoteric Enneagram, mythology and archetype, mystic linguistics, and the symbolism hidden in popular film. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Name: Gabe (Slick Dissident)
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Role: Co-host of Vibe Rant; teacher of occult symbolism & tarot

recl1wvjyRP3XfBBu.Bio: Marty Leeds is a gematria researcher, author and preacher who founded The Gnostic Church and Academy of Lord Jesus Christ in 2022, where he serves as head teacher and spiritual leader. A working minister since 2011, he is the author of more than ten books, among them the Pi & The English Alphabet series, Scripture in the Stars, The Keys to the Tarot and Gnosticism Defined: The Tenets of The Order, built around a mathematical cipher he says is hidden beneath the English alphabet. His teaching centers on Prisca Theologia, the idea of a single wisdom underlying the world's religions, drawing together gematria, Kabbalah, astrology and comparative mythology. He streams weekly sermons free through the Gnostic Academy's YouTube and Rumble channels.
recl1wvjyRP3XfBBu.Name: Marty Leeds

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Honest Research Over Celebrity Status", "body": "Marty described his last decade as scientific method applied to esoterica, with each book distilling what held up from what failed. He said he was willing to call parts of his own earlier work dead wrong and argued that doing so was the responsible thing, which he felt the truth community rarely managed. Marty also said he never pursued his work for likes or shares and judged researchers by whether their work held up years later. Chance said he was shifting from building an online platform toward work that mattered locally."}, {"title": "Astrotheology Behind the Gospel of Mark", "body": "Chance praised Marty's new documentary on the astrotheology of the Gospel of Mark, saying it was concise and accessible enough that he showed a segment to his parents over dinner. Marty said he was filling a void, since he knew of no modern researcher going that deep, and that he intended to give Revelation the same treatment. Using a star chart one of the hosts pulled up, Marty matched the beast imagery in Revelation to Draco, Ursa Major and Leo, and argued that Greek mythology was plainly built on the stars, so the Bible might be doing the same."}, {"title": "Freemasonry, Mystery and the Gatekeeper Problem", "body": "Marty defended Freemasonry as a library of ancient symbols, said the all seeing eye also appeared in Christian art, and urged listeners to read primary sources instead of repeating conspiracy claims. He said he never joined a lodge because he saw modern lodges drifting from their purpose. Gabe said he had watched several prominent lodges close. Marty argued that sealing knowledge behind mystery pushed sincere seekers to work harder, while one of the hosts argued the real problem was the middleman standing between a person and the source."}, {"title": "Psychedelics, Downloads and Receiving Knowledge", "body": "One of the hosts suggested a psychedelic age was supplying a new kind of temple for seekers and compared Dante's three realms to a DMT journey. Marty said psychedelics could be a useful tool, even in ceremony, but asked what a person actually brought back from them and cautioned against seeking everything externally. After a host described a day in 2019 when language seemed to open up, Marty said he had known similar moments of sudden understanding, called them Kabbalah, meaning receiving, and said he could take no credit for them."}, {"title": "Language, Numbers and Alchemy of the Soul", "body": "The conversation turned to English as an esoteric language rather than a slave language, with anagram examples such as silent and listen. Marty argued that numbers were supernatural because they existed everywhere in nature yet nowhere as a physical thing. Answering a Telegram voice message from Gordan Hamil, Marty said the lab was always the person and called alchemy the chemistry of the soul. He added that one must see how dark it goes before understanding how bright the light is. After he left, the hosts traded symbolic readings of Vulcanalia and the Medusa festival."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Marty Leeds, the arithmetic assessor of anagogic astrotheology, joins Vibe Rant tonight to update us about his new books, the Gnostic Academy of Lord Jesus Christ, a new documentary on the Gospel of Mark, and how life is going up nort' this summer.
